scope: Theorem 10.21 (All-scale port normalization) of the manuscript “Canonical conformal limits of subcritical FK planar maps” (preprints/Canonical-conformal-limits-of-subcritical-FK-planar-maps-September-24-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 211 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 e7dab39caf778176), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 106. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: There is a deterministic positive function B(n), tending to infinity, and constants s > 0, K < ∞ such that B(n′) B(n) ≤ K (︃ n′ n )︃s , 1 ≤ n′ ≤ n. (10.22) One can take s = p/2 and B(n) = A⌊log4 n⌋, after changing finitely many initial values. Along every deterministic sequence of diverging time units, joint crossing-data extractions in B(n) units have local comparison λD with a deterministic λ in a fixed compact subinterval of (0, ∞), after further extraction. The comparison includes all finite-cost lower certificates, complete ordered-port upper following, the simultaneous small surrounding circuits of Lemma 10.7, and finite connected systems of paths with prescribed transverse intersections. The same comparison holds on every ordinary compact patch of a conditioned finite-sphere extraction using these deterministic units and the common local kernels.
